title: Load-bearing edit guard doesn't clear after sutra_impact is run
description:
The edit guard on load-bearing files (PageRank/blast-radius threshold) blocks an Edit with "Call `sutra_impact` with symbol=X FIRST ... then retry the edit." But running sutra_impact for that symbol does not clear the block — a subsequent identical Edit is rejected with the exact same message. The only escape was SUTRA_GUARD_DISABLE=1, which defeats the point of the review handshake.

Observed 2026-08-14 during sutra/191 review follow-up: editing src/db/mod.rs (Db, pr=0.0590, blast 151) to narrow four method visibilities pub->pub(crate). Sequence:
1. Edit -> STOP, "Call sutra_impact with symbol=\"Db\" FIRST, then retry."
2. sutra_impact(symbol="Db") -> returned risk=low, 1 file touched.
3. Retry identical Edit -> STOP, same message verbatim.
4. Had to fall back to SUTRA_GUARD_DISABLE=1 to land the (verified-safe) change.

Expected: after sutra_impact is run for the named symbol, the guard should record that the impact was reviewed and permit the retried edit (some acknowledgement token / session state), OR the guard message should tell the caller the actual unblock mechanism rather than implying sutra_impact satisfies it.

Questions for triage: is the guard supposed to track "impact reviewed" state at all, or is the message misleading and the only real opt-out env-var? If it's meant to track state, what keys it (symbol name, file, session, tool-call ordering)? Does it work for MCP sutra_impact vs some other expected call? Reproduce and either wire the handshake or fix the guidance text.
execution_record: Verified the mechanism exists and works in the common case: reproduced live via the sutra-guard binary (deny on edit to a load-bearing db file; a fresh ack file at .sutra/acks/<fnv1a64(rel_path)> clears it). Confirmed root cause with `SELECT ... WHERE qualified_name='Db'` returning 10 rows across 9 files and resolve_symbol's ORDER-BY-less query landing on components.rs. Fix: added Db::symbol_definition_files(qualified_name) (SELECT DISTINCT f.path ... WHERE qualified_name=?) and changed sutra_impact in mcp.rs to touch_ack every returned file (union'd with result["file"]), exposing the set as guard_ack. Updated the tool description. Considered but rejected: (a) preferring the struct/definition over impls in resolve_symbol — still breaks when editing an impl-only file; (b) acking files_touched — wrong, those are callers and must stay guarded. Tests: added symbol_definition_files_spans_all_sites in tests/impact_test.rs (3-file Db, asserts all sites returned + empty for unknown). End-to-end: guard denies edit to src/db/graph.rs, then after acking all 9 Db sites (what fixed impact does) the retry is allowed. cargo fmt/clippy clean on changed files; impact_test/db-test/mcp_contract_test/guard lib tests all green.
root_cause: The impact ack is keyed by file, but sutra_impact only acked the single file of the symbol resolve_symbol picked. A symbol name like "Db" is shared (same qualified_name) by the struct plus its impl blocks across ~10 files, and Db::symbol_by_qualified_name runs `WHERE qualified_name=? ` with no ORDER BY, so it returns an arbitrary row (lowest rowid → src/db/components.rs). The guard blocks the file being edited (src/db/mod.rs) and names its hot symbol "Db"; sutra_impact(Db) resolved to components.rs and acked that, so the guard's per-file ack check on mod.rs never found an ack and re-denied with the identical message. The handshake was wired correctly and works when the named symbol's sole definition file equals the edited file — it silently failed whenever the name resolved to a homonym/sibling in another file.
